Review the Java Spring Boot invoice creation and billing notification change. The authenticated gateway calls the injected InvoiceService once for each unique invoice ID. Once creation succeeds, billing must eventually receive the invoice even if this process restarts or the billing endpoint is temporarily unavailable. The endpoint is an administrator-configured internal service; its POST is idempotent by the supplied invoice ID. The shown tables, listener, and configuration are the entire publication implementation. Existing access controls and schema deployment are outside this change. Review only the supplied change; do not edit files, run builds/tests, or start a workflow. Return JSON with verdict (approve or request-changes) and findings containing file, line, and reason.

files.src/main/resources/schema.sql: CREATE TABLE invoices (id varchar(80) PRIMARY KEY);

expected_findings.invariant: The transaction persists only the invoice and publishes an in-memory event. AFTER_COMMIT provides phase coupling, not durable publication: a crash after invoice commit or one failed HTTP send leaves no pending publication/replay state, violating eventual billing delivery.

The configured in-memory H2 database loses committed invoice and any pending-publication data when the process exits. DB_CLOSE_DELAY retains data across connection closes, not process restarts; durable recovery requires persistent storage.
